root_cause.text: The function `hci_le_big_create_sync` used a hardcoded constant `0x11` (17) for the maximum number of BIS entries in a stack-allocated flex array via `DEFINE_FLEX`, while the actual upper bound from `conn->num_bis` is `HCI_MAX_ISO_BIS` (31), causing a stack buffer overflow when the number of BIS entries exceeds 17.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message and CVE description state that `DEFINE_FLEX(struct hci_cp_le_big_create_sync, cp, bis, num_bis, 0x11)` allocates only 17 BIS entries, but `conn->num_bis` can be up to 31. The patch fixes this by changing `0x11` to `HCI_MAX_ISO_BIS`. The KASAN report confirms a stack-out-of-bounds write of size 31 when `num_bis` is 31.

intent_record.what: Changed the last argument of DEFINE_FLEX macro from hardcoded value 0x11 to HCI_MAX_ISO_BIS constant.
intent_record.how: The macro defines a structure with a flexible array member; the initial size for the flex array is no longer a magic number but a named constant. This may alter the allocated size if HCI_MAX_ISO_BIS differs from 0x11.
